## What does this mean?

When a generated answer guides candidate comparison, when is it trustworthy enough and when should it be reviewed?

## Why does it matter?

A reference answer can help compare candidates, but a confident wrong reference
can invert the decision. The practical question is when to accept, cross-check,
or mark a case unresolved.

## How does it work?

<ol class="hub-process hub-record-path">
<li class="hub-process-step"><strong>Question</strong><br>How reliable must a generated reference be?</li>
<li class="hub-process-step"><strong>Evidence</strong><br>3 studies addresses this question.</li>
<li class="hub-process-step"><strong>Bounded answer</strong><br>Gemini was the strongest reviewed default, but difficult and ambiguous cases still need selective escalation.</li>
</ol>

## What do we know?

Gemini was the strongest reviewed default, but difficult and ambiguous cases still need selective escalation.

**Confidence:** Moderate

## What is missing?

The 400-question review was purposive and has no organizer gold; the grounding audit focused on known failures.

The reviewed sample overweights hard questions and contains qualitative
judgments, not organizer answer-correctness labels.

**Open subquestions**

- Can a local judge reproduce the escalation set?
- How often does grounding harm an initially good answer?
